active_projects.description: Make the D2/d2-hotpath check a meaningful, deterministic regression gate before the M1 gate reads it: replace the two-sided band with a one-sided upper limit (lower is better, so a faster run never fails) plus a small positive floor whose only job is to catch the plugin not running; gate on the median of several invocations rather than one; derive the limit by a stated, repeatable method measured on a quiet machine; keep the ratchet rule of the diagnostics README (a change may not raise the limit; raising it is its own reviewed commit); and give the upper limit a negative control that bites just above it, alongside the existing diag-pairedbar control, which forces the value 100 ms past the band and so proves the gate is wired but not that it is sensitive. Measured 2026-11-19 over 83 real history entries: the band is 0.146 to 0.674 ms, cut as mean +/- 3 SD around 0.41; runs before 18:00Z had mean 0.436, SD 0.060; runs from 18:00Z had mean 0.268, SD 0.127, clustered at 0.17 to 0.25, with the lowest 0.024 ms above the lower edge. So the gate can fail on an improvement, would pass a doubling of today's typical overhead, and re-deriving the band by its own method now gives a negative lower edge. Host load was about 5 throughout, the likely but unconfirmed cause of the shift; research confirms or rules that out first, since it decides how many invocations the median needs. Edits sf1-v2/diagnostics/checks/d2-hotpath.ts, sf1-v2/diagnostics/baseline/ttft-enginebase.json, sf1-v2/diagnostics/baseline.json, both diagnostics READMEs and negctrl-diagnostics-1118.sh; touches nothing under extensions/core. Done when: bash sf1-v2/diagnose.sh passes on repeated invocations on a quiet and on a loaded machine, the new control fails where it should and nowhere else, and the M1 gate's D2 line can be read as no regression. The M1 gate depends on this

MEASURED STARTING STATE (2026-11-19): bash integration/tools/close-battery.sh exits 1 with harness_rc=1 and cross_check_rc=1. Union of failing suites across the three roots: test-routing-resolution and test-stall-reprompt-wiring (failing on ALL three roots), test-task-type-detect (opencode root only), test-orchestrate-recover-outcome (isolated root only). run-all.sh reports "75 passed, 2 failed (0 expected, 2 NEW)" per root, so these are regressions, not known exclusions. Separately, bash sf1-v2/diagnose.sh exits 1 with 11 pass, 1 fail, 2 deferred; the failure is D2/d2-hotpath.

RESEARCH MUST SETTLE THIS FIRST, because it decides whether the fix belongs in the suites or in the cut file: archived task 32's sealed three-root green record does not reproduce. specs/archive/032_make_minimal_core_test_suite_pass/records/final-20261118T201743Z.txt records 77 passed / 0 failed / 0 NEW under .claude, .opencode and isolated at 2026-11-18T20:17:43Z, and that task's summary closes with "Follow-ups: None". But test-stall-reprompt-wiring.sh line 32 resolves SKILL_MD_PATH to extensions/core/skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, and commit af77f35 ("task 17 phase 5: cut skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md to 8 KB", committed 2026-11-18 19:35:02, file mtime 19:33:04) stripped every stall_suspected, stranded_suspected and pending_stall_reprompt line from that file, replacing executable jq wiring with prose. The cut was therefore already on disk when the green record was sealed 44 minutes later, and git log shows nothing has touched that file since. Running the suite in place today gives 10 passed, 8 failed. So either the sealed evidence does not reflect the tree it claims to attest, or run-core-suite-three-roots.sh's scratch copies diverge from the committed tree. Determine which. A green record that cannot be reproduced is a verification-integrity defect in the merge gate itself, and matters more than the two test fixes. Do not weaken any assertion to close it.

ITEM 1 -- the two suites failing on all three roots, both named in task 32's original list of 29:
  - test-stall-reprompt-wiring (8 failures): skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md no longer reads stall_suspected or stranded_suspected; the Move 3 region is missing the suppression guard, does not key its guard on stall_reprompted, does not OR the two signals together, and does not write pending_stall_reprompt. The eighth failure cannot extract the Move 3 jq program from SKILL.md at all. Note the suite's own failure text, "the signal is dead again", and the untracked stall_suspected file at the repository root. Record exactly one disposition: restore the wiring the 8 KB cut removed, or re-site the assertions if the cut was deliberate and the mechanism legitimately moved -- naming where it moved to.
  - test-routing-resolution: Assert 3 (branch-aware) -- SKILL.md's Move 2 dispatch site does not reference the row's resolved .agent field.

ITEM 2 -- the root-sensitivity misclassification that close-battery.sh's empirical cross-root cross-check caught, which named its own remedy: test-orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh is classed STABLE (root-invariant) in extensions/core/scripts/tests/suite-root-sensitivity.data but produced claude=PASS opencode=PASS isolated=FAIL. Re-run integration/tools/derive-root-sensitivity.sh, correct the classification, re-commit. Also account for test-task-type-detect, which failed only on the opencode root. Both are root-varying results that the static preflight did not catch, so check whether the static half needs the same correction.

ITEM 3 -- re-baseline D2/d2-hotpath, which blocks the M1 gate task's own done-condition ("show by tiers D2 and D4 no regression against the recorded baseline"). sf1-v2/diagnostics/checks/d2-hotpath.ts passes only when the paired median diff lands inside the recorded CI95 band [0.393, 0.462] ms, a two-sided window of roughly +/-0.034 ms on a sub-millisecond measurement, with direction "none" in baseline.json so either side fails. sf1-v2/diagnostics/history.jsonl shows 15 of the last 20 runs outside that band on BOTH sides (0.375 and 0.385 low, 0.585 high), plus two runs at 100.46 that are the diag-pairedbar negative control firing. Re-record the baseline with a tolerance reflecting the measurement's actual variance, preserve the ratchet rule in sf1-v2/diagnostics/README.md, and keep the negative control biting.

DONE WHEN: bash integration/tools/close-battery.sh is green -- harness exit 0 AND the empirical cross-root cross-check passing -- and bash sf1-v2/diagnose.sh exits 0 across repeated consecutive runs rather than a single lucky one. rules: New behaviour defaults off; with the task flag off the request is byte-identical to SF-1.
Every guard has a negative control that bites where it claims and nowhere else.
Edits go to the source tree; `.claude/` and `.opencode/` are regenerated, never hand-edited.
Both trees come from the same source at the same revision.
Nothing is added without the failure it prevents; nothing is ported without a user.

Extension code lives outside the plugin. `sf1 ext` is its own module, reached from the launcher by one lazily imported branch; a plain `sf1` launch in a project with no ledger does one file check and nothing else.

No new subsystem in the plugin. Hooks, permissions and instructions go through the existing `claudehooks.ts`, `claudeperms.ts` and `claudeproject.ts`; the only new engine code is the child-session gates, the task flag and the two bridged events.
Engine touch is counted: every change reports lines added under `sf1-v2/` and new `SF1_` variables.
Cost is paid at load, not at run; the loaded set is fixed for a session, and the brief is assembled once per launch.
Ratchet, not target: a change may not raise a baseline, and raising one is a separate, reviewed commit that says why.
conventions: **Before**: D0-D3 pass against the committed baseline for the current engine base.

**In every PR**: the entry script's pass/fail lines beside the `run-tests.sh` lines, and what D0, D2 and D3 moved by.
**On a new engine base** (PR #3 merging is the next): record the baseline again before measuring anything against it.

batches.rationale:
First, and three tasks in one sequenced dispatch. The first two share a file tree and are sequenced by an edge for that reason. Both are the opening pair of vision/milestones.md's order: milestone 1, measurement trusted (G4), then milestone 2, translation trusted (G2). Both are admissible from this repository today -- no hold, no external owner, nothing wanted from the SF-1 side -- so this batch is the move on the list rather than a recorded intention.

The batch exists because the territory overlaps, which was measured this pass rather than assumed. sf1-v2/diagnostics/run.ts is the single registration site for every check, importing each one by name from checks/*.ts, so a task adding three checks and a task changing how one check is invoked both land in it. sf1-v2/diagnostics/baseline.json holds one checks object, which the D2 task rewrites for its new limit and which the translator checks have to be recorded in before either is done. Both READMEs carry the ratchet rule a limit is read under, and both tasks add a negative control beside the existing negctrl scripts. Shared territory is a reason to batch and never a reason to separate, so they run as one dispatch serialized to width 1.

The edge runs D2 first, and the direction is not arbitrary. The D2 task is the one that rewrites the baseline's D2 rows and the READMEs' statement of how a limit is derived and ratcheted; the translator checks then add three rows and a committed per-extension digest under exactly that rule. Reversed, the D2 task would rewrite the README section the translator checks had just extended, and the new checks would be recorded against a derivation rule about to change underneath them. The D2 task is also the one the M1 gate names as a prerequisite, so putting it first serves the gate as well as the file tree.

The D2 half is worth doing on its own merits, and its own measurement is why. Over 83 real history entries the current two-sided band is 0.146 to 0.674 ms, cut as mean +/- 3 SD around 0.41; runs before 18:00Z averaged 0.436 with SD 0.060, runs from 18:00Z averaged 0.268 with SD 0.127 and clustered at 0.17 to 0.25, the lowest only 0.024 ms above the lower edge. A band like that can fail on an improvement, would pass a doubling of today's typical overhead, and re-derived by its own method now gives a negative lower edge. A one-sided upper limit on the median of several invocations, a small positive floor whose only job is to catch the plugin not running, and a control that bites just above the limit are what turn the D2 line the gate reads into a claim worth reading -- the existing diag-pairedbar control forces the value 100 ms past the band, so it proves the gate is wired but not that it is sensitive. Research settles whether the host load of about 5 explains the shift before anything is derived, since that decides how many invocations the median needs.

The translator half is the cheapest trust the project can buy: a census of every frontmatter key, tool name and deploy-root path form against the rule table, with translator.ts made to throw on an unmapped key instead of passing it through; a determinism check translating the same source twice into scratch roots and comparing byte for byte against a committed digest; and permission equality derived independently from the .claude and .opencode trees. Corpus is extensions/core, no network, nothing needed from the SF-1 side, and each check gets a control that bites where it claims and nowhere else.

The comparison instrument rides third in this batch by the owner's choice, sequenced behind the translator checks by an edge added for that purpose. It shares no file territory with the diagnostics pair: it writes a new comparison script, gets the Claude Code arm of harness/fixes-1116/remeasure/ running on Linux where it carries a macOS sandbox profile, and writes its output in the run-record format of integration/extension-system.md section 10.4. The edge is an ordering convenience so one dispatch carries all three, and it costs the instrument a wait it does not technically need. This is milestone 3 of vision/milestones.md: a script that takes two completed runs of the same task, one under sf1 on OpenCode and one under Claude Code, and writes one paired record with a structural diff and one timing method, every difference classified expected or unexplained. The M1 gate depends on it by a real edge, so the gate cannot fall back to a by-hand comparison. Its negative control is a fixture pair carrying one injected difference, which must be reported unexplained.

batches.description: Invert the translator to prove the forward pass, then widen both over the whole port inventory
batches.rationale:
Second, and the first batch on this list that is not dispatchable today -- by one edge, not by any external block. It depends on the translator checks in the first batch for the census and the diagnostics registration it extends, so it sits in wave 3 and becomes admissible the moment that batch lands. Nothing in it is owned on the SF-1 side.

It completes milestone 2 with properties T3 and T4 of vision/parity.md section 2.2: an inverse pass beside sf1-v2/opencode-plugin/src/translator.ts for every mapped row, with each lossy row declared by name -- the two deny rules the forward pass adds on non-root agents, and a tier word resolved to a concrete model id -- then a round-trip check that translate-then-invert reproduces the source byte for byte except for those declared rows, with a control in which a rule edited to drop a field must break the round trip. T4 then takes the census, determinism and round-trip checks from extensions/core out to every extension in integration/port-inventory.md, reporting unmapped constructs as a count that ratchets down.

The inverse is a proof instrument first and an import path second, which is what keeps design choice A2 intact: the Claude format stays the source. That also settles where open question 2 of vision/milestones.md gets its answer -- the neutral authoring format is reopened only if the census shows constructs the rule table cannot express in either direction, so the census has to run before the question can be decided rather than the other way round.

Alone in its batch rather than folded into the first, even though it shares the diagnostics tree and the translator with its predecessor, because the first batch is what can be dispatched now and this is what follows it. Keeping the boundary visible is the point of the order; the edge, not array position, is what actually serializes them.

batches.description: Stand up the nix dev shell; its venv half cannot finish until the engine wheel arrives from Oliver
batches.rationale:
Fourth, behind three batches that can be driven to their done-conditions and ahead of the whole harness-integration chain, which cannot be dispatched at all. That position is exactly its shape: genuinely half-dispatchable. The dev-shell half needs nothing external -- nix and uv are on the host, node and python3 resolve, and there is no flake.nix at the repository root yet, so the Python 3.13 / uv / Node shell can be written, entered and committed today. The half it is actually judged on cannot be finished: the documented command has to install the SF-1 engine wheel (engram.server, 6.7.6) into the lab venv and point SF1_ENGINE_PY at that interpreter so sf1-v2/run-tests.sh and the negctrl-*.sh scripts start the Python suites on a machine other than Oliver's, and it is done only when those suites start and the recorded known-failing baseline is re-read against the result.

The wheel is absent, and that was established by four independent checks in the previous pass rather than re-measured in this one: no .whl matching engram or ngrm anywhere under the home tree or in this repository; the lab venv the scripts default to holding exactly pip and nothing else, with import engram raising ModuleNotFoundError; the vendored mcp-ko-server source at 5.6.0 whose ko_write accepts neither event_date nor no_cross_supersede, two of the keywords sapience_lab_mcp.py's preflight demands, so it cannot stand in for the wheel; and a public index carrying only ngrm 0.0.1 and engram 0.1.0a1, so it cannot be self-served. What was re-confirmed this pass is that issue #26, where the wheel was requested once, is still open.

It carries EXT-BLOCKED for that reason, while differing from the SF-1-side entries in who holds the remedy: not another clone, but a wheel handed over on an open issue. It stays at not_started rather than held, because the shell half really is admissible and a hold would put it out of reach of every ordinary command. vision/milestones.md places it on no critical path, and the dependency graph agrees in both directions: nothing in the chain waits on it and it waits on nothing here.

One clause of its done-condition is still unverified: test_dispatch_memory.py does not exist anywhere in this checkout, and is most likely delivered by the dispatch-memory work on PR #38 -- confirmed open and unmerged again this pass -- rather than by this task, which would make that clause wait on the PR as well as on the wheel. That reading is inference from the filename and the PR's subject, not measurement, and should be confirmed before this task is planned.

batches.description: The M1 gate -- two local prerequisites now, plus the held SF-1-side host plugin it cannot clear
batches.rationale:
Fifth, and the head of the harness-integration chain rather than the head of this list. Two local prerequisites are open, one of them new. The D2 hot-path limit in the first batch has been a prerequisite by edge for a pass already; the comparison instrument in the same first batch became one when that task was created, and it is the more consequential of the two, because it decides whether this gate is judged by a script or by hand. Both are in the gate's dependency list, both are local, and both are dispatchable now -- which makes this the one place on the list where local work genuinely moves the chain's head closer.

It also corrects a claim earlier passes carried: that every instrument this gate needs already exists on disk. D2's exists but does not yet discriminate, and the paired-record instrument does not exist at all. Milestone 4 of vision/milestones.md is written accordingly -- one task completing on each harness with a paired record and no unexplained difference, a task started on one harness finishing on the other, and flag-off byte identity -- and the paired record in that sentence is the first batch's deliverable.

What has not changed is the external block, and it still decides whether this is a dispatch or an order to run in. The gate waits on the SF-1 host plugin and launcher changes (issue #21), held here, worked in another clone, and carried on PR #37, which was confirmed open and unmerged this pass. So clearing both local prerequisites does not make this runnable: three things have to land, two of them from here. Everything below inherits the same wait through it.

Alone rather than batched with the loader's launcher half below, and not merely because an edge sequences the two. The loader split means every manifest addition is only what M1 proved necessary, so the launcher half's content is not decided until this gate has produced its measurements; a single dispatch admitting both would plan the second against a specification the first had not yet written. They share no file territory either -- this gate drives one task end to end in a separate project directory, never this checkout, while the launcher half edits sf1-v2/ and the manifest.

The work itself is a measurement, not a deliverable: one real task driven from research to completed under sf1, the same task re-run under Claude Code from the .claude copy, statuses, artifacts and commit messages compared, a task started under one harness shown finishing under the other, and the flag-off byte-identity control confirmed with no task tree deployed. Both arms are timed by the remeasure harness's one timing method under the scored run profile, so the result carries over to the goal 11 sealed test rather than being redone there. D1 carries the flag-off byte identity, D0 the brief, agents, skills, listing descriptions and context files inside budget, D2 and D4 no regression against the recorded baseline, and D3 hook time inside the ratcheted hard limit -- p95 and worst case, count-exempt hooks included -- which under Q2 fails this gate when exceeded instead of being reported beside it.

roadmap_milestones.title: The extension system
roadmap_milestones.aim: A loader that loads, unloads and syncs extensions into both deploy trees from one ledger.
roadmap_milestones.gate: Load, unload and sync round-trip both trees with no orphan files; a failed load leaves both trees unchanged; with no extensions loaded, behaviour equals M1.

batches.description: Add the loader's launcher half and its manifest additions, the rest of M2, behind the gate
batches.rationale:
M2's remainder, and behind the gate by the same Q3 ruling that put the file-level half ahead of it. That half has landed, so this batch is exactly what the split deliberately held back: everything that generates runtime configuration, reaches into the launcher, or adds to the manifest. The manifest additions are specified as only what M1 proved necessary, which is why this half genuinely cannot be written before the gate rather than merely being tidier after it.

What it adds on top of the ledger and the file operations: harness hooks (with a guard's unattended default as a field on its hook entry, and a field marking a core-owned hook exempt from the five-hooks-per-call limit), permission rules, a brief section, MCP servers, required binaries and a top-level interview key holding question lists per task type; the dispatch builder writing each task record's forcing_data into every dispatch file; load extended to check the five-blocking-hooks-per-call limit, the required binaries, each brief-section heading against the ritual filter drop list, and that no extension hook opens a network connection on the tool-call path, with a hook that does refused at load; the kernel brief and per-extension sections assembled once per launch so the cached prefix is stable; and sf1 --target claude as the fail-safe launch.

Two of its deliverables are what the batch below is built on: the manifest's hook-cap-exemption field, which the sandbox guard's hook registration uses, and the load-time check that the guard is present, registered and unaltered by anything sf1 ext sync just touched, failing a load exactly as a missing required binary does. The guard itself is a separate task deliberately, since it consumes the exemption field rather than defining it.

The engine rules bind hardest here, because this is the only task in the plan that reaches into the launcher at all. sf1 ext stays its own module outside the plugin, reached by one lazily imported branch, so a plain sf1 launch in a project with no ledger does one file check and nothing else. No new subsystem goes into the plugin: hooks, permissions and instructions go through the existing claudehooks.ts, claudeperms.ts and claudeproject.ts. Every launch-time step finishes before the prewarm starts the server and adds nothing to cold start. And the PR reports lines added under sf1-v2/ and new SF1_ variables, adds the with-ledger launch arm to D4, and states what D0, D2 and D3 moved by. Its research closes one open design point by probe -- whether the generated runtime config can set a model per agent -- and it checks Gate M2's last clause: with no extensions loaded, behaviour equals M1.

roadmap_milestones.title: The extensions in use
roadmap_milestones.aim: Port the six extensions in use; each passes the budgets and runs one task of its type on both harnesses.
roadmap_milestones.gate: The six extensions load together within budget on both trees with no command or keyword collision; one task of each type completes on OpenCode.

batches.description: Ship the guard the loader refuses to load without, then port the six extensions behind it
batches.rationale:
M3, and one batch rather than two because neither member can load anything until the other exists. The loader fails a load outright when the extension filesystem-read sandbox guard is missing or altered, and the extension port's whole gate is six extensions loading together within budget on both trees -- so the port is not merely tidier after the guard, it is unrunnable before it. A serializing edge carries that: the port depends on the guard, which drains in the earlier wave.

The guard in turn depends on the loader's launcher half, since it registers its hook through the exemption field that half adds, and on the host-plugin task, for the fail-closed child-session gate it wires into -- making it the tenth such gate and the only one that must fire in a child session and block rather than skip when it cannot resolve whether it is in one. Its file is sited outside anything sf1 ext sync can remove or alter, which is what makes the loader's check meaningful, and it carries one negative control per rule. That second predecessor is the externally owned host-plugin task, so this batch inherits the clone-boundary wait directly as well as through the gate.

The port then runs in the fixed order git-flow, typescript, python, slidev, present, founder, with present before founder, each inside the per-extension budgets and each running one task of its type on both harnesses; forcing questions move to the root session as manifest interview entries or user_decision hand-backs, confirming the provisional 28 / 22 / 36 split file by file. Each extension's PR states what D0, D2 and D3 moved by with it loaded, and the port adds the six-extension arm to D4. The sapience extension is deliberately not among them; its two functions are the dispatch memory script in M1 and the completion notes in M4, both provided inside SF-1.

batches.description: Write the rules that postdate design.md back into it, once each has actually shipped
batches.rationale:
Last, and deliberately so. Several rules were settled after design.md was written -- the model allow-list and its GLM-pin negative control, the filesystem-read sandbox guard with its core-only placement and negative controls, the manifest hook-cap-exemption field, the guard's tenth, fail-closed entry in the child-session table, and the hard hook-time limit of Q2 together with the diagnostics tiers as standing checks -- and each lives today only in the task description of whichever task implements it, or in the roadmap's own Settled decisions. This batch is where they become part of the document the rest of the port is read against.

Two of its predecessors have already landed, which makes its eventual content more settled than it was: the translator shipped the model allow-list and its GLM-pin control, and tier D3 produced the hook-time figure and the method behind it, so neither has to be written down from a plan any more. What it still waits on is the loader's launcher half, the sandbox guard, the extension port, and the externally owned host-plugin task -- that last one by a direct edge of its own, not merely by a path through the other three.

It is alone in its batch because its content is not decided until those predecessors have landed: it records what they actually built, not what they were asked to build. No ruling in the document is reversed here, which is why this task carries no gate of its own and why it is safe to leave until the end.

Its ordering against the extension port is carried by the graph rather than by array position, and the reason it belongs after the port is a read/write conflict on a single file: the port is specified by design.md section 5.10 and reads part 5 throughout, while this task rewrites part 5, adding the sandbox-guard subsection and the hook-cap-exemption field. Left unedged the two would share a wave, and a dispatch admitting both would have edited the port's specification underneath the port. The edge serializes them in this direction rather than the reverse: this task documents the loader, guard and host-plugin work and no part of the port, so amending the document first would give the port nothing it needs, while its own content is only settled once everything it records has landed.

roadmap_milestones.title: Fit with SF-1's memory
roadmap_milestones.aim: Small joins that stop the task layer and SF-1's memory contradicting each other; needs only M1.
roadmap_milestones.gate: An autonomous task run creates no knowledge objects on its own; `STATE.md` and `state.json` never disagree about a task; no keypress gate stalls an unattended run.
